elements.quote: A systematic review with metaanalysis of prevalence was conducted in October 2023
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states it is a systematic review.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to find out the prevalence and factors that favoured the development of depression in nursing students during the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a clear main objective (prevalence and factors related to depression during COVID-19).

elements.quote: Quantitative primary studies using anonymous scales and surveys to assess the prevalence of depression in nursing students in the last 3 years were included.
elements.reason: The abstract provides inclusion criteria (e.g., quantitative primary studies; anonymous scales/surveys; last 3 years) but does not explicitly state main exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: using Pubmed, CINAHL and Scopus as the data sources used for the search. This review was conducted in October 2023
elements.reason: The abstract names the information sources (PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus) and gives when they were searched (October 2023).
No methods to assess risk of bias in included studies are reported in the abstract evidence provided.
The abstract evidence does not describe the methods used to present and synthesize results (e.g., meta-analytic approach details).

elements.quote: The final set of articles was N = 12... The total sample of students in the meta-analysis was n = 4,479 with a prevalence value of 32% (CI95% 22%-42%). Affected students are characterised by young, female students.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (N=12), the total participant sample in the meta-analysis (n=4,479), and summarizes relevant characteristics (young, female students).

elements.quote: The total sample of students in the meta-analysis was n = 4,479 with a prevalence value of 32% (CI95% 22%-42%).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcome (prevalence of depression), including effect estimate with CI and sample size.

elements.quote: with a prevalence value of 32% (CI95% 22%-42%).
elements.reason: Because a meta-analysis was conducted, the abstract reports the summary estimate (32%) with its 95% confidence interval.
The abstract does not indicate that any comparative group analysis was performed (no direction of effect or favored group described).
The abstract evidence provided does not explicitly summarize important limitations (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision) of the included evidence.

elements.quote: In conclusion, students, especially female students, are at high risk of depression due to social isolation. In addition, coping techniques were inadequate and future strategies to prevent this situation should be considered.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an interpretation of the results and states implications for prevention/strategies.
No primary source of funding is reported in the abstract evidence provided.
The abstract evidence provided does not report any register name or registration number.

elements.quote: The pandemic meant a change in academic approach. This had an impact on the mental health of students, leading to, among other problems, depressive disorders.
elements.reason: Describes the current situation/knowledge context that COVID-19 affected students’ mental health and depression, but it does not explicitly state important uncertainties or specific gaps in existing knowledge.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to find out the prevalence and factors that favoured the development of depression in nursing students during the COVID-19 pandemic. A systematic review with metaanalysis of prevalence was conducted in October 2023, using Pubmed, CINAHL and Scopus as the data sources used for the search.
elements.reason: Explains the purpose/need for the review by stating the aim (identify prevalence and factors) and that a systematic review with meta-analysis was conducted to address it.
No evidence retrieved describing prior similar systematic reviews or explaining why the current review is needed in relation to existing reviews (e.g., updates/replications with citations).
The criterion concerns intervention effects and mechanisms of action; this review is described as a systematic review and meta-analysis of prevalence (not an intervention effect review).

The criterion concerns complex interventions and a logic model; the retrieved evidence indicates the study is a prevalence meta-analysis rather than a complex intervention/delivery-context evaluation.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to analyse the factors that favoured the development of depression in university nursing students during the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as to estimate the prevalence of this disorder in this university group.
elements.reason: The review objective is explicitly stated (“aim of this study was to analyse…” and “estimate the prevalence…”), but it is not presented using a relevant question-formulation framework.

elements.quote: Asystematic review of the scientific literature and a meta-analysis of prevalence was carried out for this article.
elements.reason: The review is a meta-analysis of prevalence rather than an intervention effects review, so planned intervention comparisons using PICO (or variant) are not applicable.

elements.quote: Inclusion criteria: primary quantitative studies; the articles that were included were in English and Spanish; the design had to be quantitative; without geographical restriction by country; the study population of the articles was focused on nursing students suffering from depression at the time of COVID-19; and finally, they had to have been published in the last 3 years, i.e. between 2020 and 2023 which is when the COVID-19 pandemic took place.
elements.reason: Eligibility inclusion criteria specify study population, study design (quantitative), and timing context (during COVID-19 timeframe) and some language. However, the evidence does not specify all relevant study-characteristic components requested (e.g., eligible study settings and any follow-up requirements), nor does it describe how studies were grouped for syntheses.

elements.quote: the articles that were included were in English and Spanish; ... they had to have been published in the last 3 years, i.e. between 2020 and 2023 which is when the COVID-19 pandemic took place.
elements.reason: The review specifies report characteristics including language (English and Spanish) and dissemination year/time window (2020 to 2023).
The evidence provided lists inclusion/exclusion criteria but does not distinguish exclusions due to outcomes not being measured versus outcomes not being reported.
No evidence is provided that the review specified the groups used in each synthesis and linked them to comparisons in the review objectives.
Although inclusion/exclusion criteria are described, the evidence provided does not provide rationales for notable restrictions on study eligibility.

elements.quote: The electronic databases used for the bibliographic search were: Pubmed, CINAHL and Scopus in accordance with the recommendations made in the declaration Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) [33]. The following search equation was used: '(undergraduate nurses OR nursing students) AND depression AND (COVID19 OR Sars-CoV-2)'. The descriptors of the search equation were extracted through the thesaurus Medical Subject Heading (MeSH) and its equivalent in Spanish. The search was conducted in October 2023.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports when the search was conducted (last searched/consulted date): October 2023.
Although Pubmed, CINAHL, and Scopus are named, no search interface/platform details or coverage dates are reported for each database.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories are reported as being searched, so no names or date restrictions are provided.
No websites, search engines, or other online sources (with names and URLs) are reported as searched.
The evidence does not mention any organizations or manufacturers contacted to identify studies.
The evidence does not describe any types of individuals contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: Once the aforementioned search criteria had been applied, the bibliography was selected in the following steps: reading the title, reading the abstract, reading the full text and finally, reviewing the references included in the selected articles.
elements.reason: The manuscript indicates that references within selected articles were reviewed, but it does not clearly specify the full types of reference lists examined (e.g., backward/forward citation approaches) beyond this statement.

elements.quote: Finally, by performing a reverse search analysing the bibliography of these 11 articles, 3 more were retrieved, leaving a final sample of n = 14 articles.
elements.reason: A reverse (backward) search using the bibliography is described, but the seed reports/citation index/platform used and the search date are not reported.
No journals or conference proceedings consulted are reported, and no source names, dates covered, or search methods for such sources are provided.

elements.quote: The following search equation was used: '(undergraduate nurses OR nursing students) AND depression AND (COVID19 OR Sars-CoV-2)'. elements.reason: A single search equation and brief descriptor source are reported, but the full, database-by-database search strategies (as actually run) for each database/register/website (e.g., PubMed vs. CINAHL vs. Scopus syntax/fields/commands) are not provided.
No search limits (e.g., dates, language filters, study design filters) are reported as part of the search strategy, nor any justification tying limits to eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: The following search equation was used: '(undergraduate nurses OR nursing students) AND depression AND (COVID19 OR Sars-CoV-2)'.
elements.reason: A clear conceptual structure using AND/OR terms is reported, so the criterion for describing an alternative final conceptual structure when the search was not based on PICO is not applicable based on the provided evidence.

elements.quote: According to recent studies, the risk factors that predispose nursing students to suffer from depression are very heterogeneous. In Spain, an increase in depression was observed in comparison with other countries (Fig 3). This increase may have been caused by the way the pandemic developed, with a very high increase in patients with COVID-19, suspected cases and deaths during the different waves in the country. All of this obviously had an impact on a personal level, increasing concern, anxiety, stress and finally depression about the possibility of infecting themselves or their loved ones.
elements.reason: The Discussion interprets the findings by comparing them with other countries and “recent studies,” and provides explanations in relation to the broader evidence base.

The retrieved Discussion content does not describe limitations of the evidence included in the review. The only related material (e.g., critical reading for potential biases) is mentioned in a non-Discussion section and does not constitute a discussion of limitations of the included evidence.
The retrieved evidence mentions that biases and limitations could be discussed, but it does not provide any specific limitations of the review processes or their discussion.
Because no specific review-process limitations are discussed in the retrieved evidence, the potential impact of each limitation is also not reported.
